title: County Commissioner, District 1
notes: Elected only by voters in the district. No term limit. Lawsuit: In February 2023 the City of South Bend and two county voters, Warren and Iris Outlaw, sued the State of Indiana Election Commission in Marion Superior Court 11 (cause 49D11-2302-PL-005795). The complaint challenges the state laws that give St. Joseph County district-only elections for commissioners and for the county council, including the changes House Enrolled Act 1285 of 2022 made to the population range in IC 36-2-2-4(c) and 36-2-3-4(c). It argues they are special legislation barred by Indiana Constitution Article 4, sections 22 and 23, and that they also violate Article 1, section 23 and Article 2, section 1. In April 2023 the Election Commission moved to dismiss. ABC57 reported that the motion argued the Commission does not run or enforce the law, so it was the wrong party to sue, and that the plaintiffs had not shown any actual harm. In May 2023 the City amended the complaint to add as defendants the St. Joseph County Board of Commissioners and commissioners Carl Baxmeyer, Deb Fleming and Derek Dieter, the St. Joseph County Council and its members, and the St. Joseph County Election Board (ABC57, May 22, 2023; court docket). The defendants opposed the claims: the docket shows their cross-motion for summary judgment and a joint reply in January 2025. The text of the briefs is not posted on MyCase, so the guide does not describe either side's arguments beyond the complaint and the motion to dismiss. The court held a bench trial on Feb 6, 2026 and entered final judgment on Apr 14, 2026 (amended Apr 21, typo fixes only). The court record lists the challenged statutes as IC 36-2-2-4(a)(2) and (c), 36-2-2-5(d)(2), 36-2-3-2(b) and 36-2-3-4(a)(2) and (c). The order's text is not posted publicly, so its scope is known only from news reports: ABC57 reported on Apr 22, 2026 that a judge ruled the district method of electing commissioners violates the free-and-equal-elections guarantee, and 95.3 MNC reported on May 14, 2026 that the county council passed a resolution encouraging the county to appeal "a recent Indianapolis judge's ruling" on the nine-member council structure, which the station described as finding that structure illegal. The Election Commission and other defendants appealed to the Indiana Supreme Court (26S-PL-00156, filed May 14, 2026); the appeal was fully briefed on Oct 2, 2026 and is pending. The Nov 2026 election was held under the district system.
